# Onboarding-trigger result at the May 12, 2023 company all-hands

**Event:** Company all-hands, May 12, 2023, 2:00 p.m.  
**Presentation:** “Mid-segment churn investigation Feb-Apr 2023 — what we learned”  
**Audience:** Approximately 140 people. The slot comprised 15 minutes of presentation and 10 minutes of Q&A.

## Result and presentation framing

The onboarding-trigger experiment (EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger) compared an activation-keyed onboarding touch with the fixed calendar-day-7 timing for the mid-segment cohort. The contemporaneous experiment readout reported pooled week-1 retention **3.1 percentage points higher in treatment than control** across two cohorts (**n=420, p=0.04**). The experiment had been confirmed on the second cohort before the all-hands; the rollout followed on April 10.

At this all-hands, the result was presented as part of the **method learned from the mid-segment churn investigation**, not as a postmortem or a standalone victory claim. The sequence emphasized was: define the cohort, enumerate plausible hypotheses, use a cadence of checks to rule them out, run the A/B test, then wait for a stabilization cohort before acting as though the result is settled. The discussion was framed around the investigation process and what to document, rather than drama around a single outcome.

## Explicit recognition in this presentation

The presenter explicitly named **Owen Pham** and **Ines Kovac** during the all-hands. This records recognition given in this specific presentation; it does not establish a general credit policy, exhaustive contributor list, or universal allocation of credit for the experiment or framework.

## Source note

This note is based on contemporaneous internal records: the May 10 deck-preparation entry identifies the presentation title and intended “what we saw / what was noise / what changed / what rule we use now” framing [1]; the May 12 pre-meeting entry records the 15-minute talk, 10-minute Q&A, and intent to name Owen and Ines [2]; the May 12 post-meeting account records the approximately 140-person audience, the method sequence, and that Owen and Ines were named [3]. The pooled experiment result is corroborated by the April 3 result entry, which gives +3.1 points, p=0.04, n=420 across two cohorts [4]. These are contemporaneous internal logs, including a presenter’s post-meeting account, rather than a verbatim transcript or preserved slide text; the framing and recognition are therefore reported as documented recollection, not quoted speech.

### Record references

[1] Internal event record, 2023-05-10 15:00 (record `58d2a813-7d0e-4e2b-980c-190301c90e82`), deck preparation and title.  
[2] Internal event record, 2023-05-12 08:30 (record `4b06b6b8-f629-4427-87d8-30b56f186325`), all-hands preparation.  
[3] Internal event record, 2023-05-12 14:00 (record `e6b6a59e-9e02-4996-a729-8baa04547e36`), post-meeting account.

# Onboarding-trigger result at the May 12, 2023 company all-hands

**Event:** Company all-hands, May 12, 2023, 2:00 p.m.  
**Presentation:** “Mid-segment churn investigation Feb-Apr 2023 — what we learned”  
**Audience:** Approximately 140 people. The slot comprised 15 minutes of presentation and 10 minutes of Q&A.

## Result and presentation framing

The onboarding-trigger experiment (EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger) compared an activation-keyed onboarding touch with the fixed calendar-day-7 timing for the mid-segment cohort. The contemporaneous experiment readout reported pooled week-1 retention **3.1 percentage points higher in treatment than control** across two cohorts (**n=420, p=0.04**). The experiment had been confirmed on the second cohort before the all-hands; the rollout followed on April 10.

At this all-hands, the result was presented as part of the **method learned from the mid-segment churn investigation**, not as a postmortem or a standalone victory claim. The sequence emphasized was: define the cohort, enumerate plausible hypotheses, use a cadence of checks to rule them out, run the A/B test, then wait for a stabilization cohort before acting as though the result is settled. The discussion was framed around the investigation process and what to document, rather than drama around a single outcome.

## Explicit recognition in this presentation

The presenter explicitly named **Owen Pham** and **Ines Kovac** during the all-hands. This records recognition given in this specific presentation; it does not establish a general credit policy, exhaustive contributor list, or universal allocation of credit for the experiment or framework.

This note is based on contemporaneous internal records: the May 10 deck-preparation entry identifies the presentation title and intended “what we saw / what was noise / what changed / what rule we use now” framing [1]; the May 12 pre-meeting entry records the 15-minute talk, 10-minute Q&A, and intent to name Owen and Ines [2]; the May 12 post-meeting account records the approximately 140-person audience, the method sequence, and that Owen and Ines were named [3]. The pooled experiment result is corroborated by the April 3 result entry, which gives +3.1 points, p=0.04, n=420 across two cohorts [4]. These are contemporaneous internal logs, including a presenter’s post-meeting account, rather than a verbatim transcript or preserved slide text; the framing and recognition are therefore reported as documented recollection, not quoted speech.
